correctness.rationale: For all three positive shore orders, any mixed shore in a period-two state must be frozen: a strict vote would erase heterogeneity irreversibly. One flipping shore is impossible due its unchanged external neighbors. Two flipping shores must have opposite phases and equal sizes, and their frozen third shore has exactly binomial-window admissible assignments \(|2h-c|<t\). Three flipping shores require one strictly largest shore and give one orbit. All cases are disjoint and exhaustive; integer parity endpoints are strict. Independently, occupancy enumeration checks 729 triples (sizes 1 through 9), and direct labelled iteration checks 646680 configurations over 80 triples. The proof, not those finite checks, establishes the unrestricted formula.

originality.rationale: The new unequal-shore count is not implied by the accessible general period-two theorem or the irreversible complete-multipartite conversion literature. A directly overlapping earlier exact formula for equal-size multipartite graphs covers the all-equal specialization, which is expressly excluded from the novelty claim. The proof resolves the unequal three-shore case with a strict binomial window and unique-largest trichotomy. The earliest general threshold papers were not available in full, leaving a documented historical priority risk.

value.rationale: The number of primitive period-two orbits is a natural invariant of finite deterministic opinion dynamics. The result gives a complete classification across arbitrary positive tripartite shore sizes; exact imbalance matters qualitatively. Pairwise distinct sizes yield exactly one cycle, equal sizes of two shores unlock a binomial central-window family, and balanced equal sizes have exponential counts. This explains a structural transition in recurrent disagreement, beyond the universal period bound or an unmotivated small finite computation.
